```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
source("R/config.R")
source("R/analyze.R")
source("R/plots.R")

clean  <- read_csv(CLEAN_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)
log    <- read_csv(CLEAN_LOG_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)
season <- recreation_season(clean, RECREATION_MONTHS)
sites  <- site_exceedance(season, SINGLE_SAMPLE_LIMIT)
yearly <- yearly_exceedance(season, SINGLE_SAMPLE_LIMIT)
```

## Data

Results were downloaded from the Water Quality Portal for all Indiana E. coli
samples collected between `r START_DATE` and `r END_DATE`. The cleaned dataset
contains `r format(nrow(clean), big.mark = ",")` samples from
`r format(n_distinct(clean$site_id), big.mark = ",")` monitoring sites.

```{r cleaning-log}
kable(log, col.names = c("Cleaning step", "Rows remaining"), format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Results

### Which sites exceed the limit most often?

```{r top-sites, fig.height=6}
plot_top_sites(sites)
```

### Is there a seasonal pattern?

```{r monthly, fig.height=5}
plot_monthly_distribution(clean, SINGLE_SAMPLE_LIMIT)
```

### Has it changed over time?

```{r yearly, fig.height=4}
plot_yearly_exceedance(yearly)
```
